name: Bot states: overnight to in service
subject: A Coco bot in the Chicago pilot
description: The states a bot moves through on the way out, from the secure area at dawn to working at a merchant. Hands over to the Regulatory Compliance model once the bot is in service, and to the Undeployment model at end of service. Exception states sit below the main run.

states.label: Overnight in the secure area
states.description: Where the day starts. The bot is inside a private secure area, indoor or outdoor, with the overnight power state the Undeployment SOP set for it.
states.rule: Nothing is left sitting in public overnight

states.label: Overnight at the merchant
states.description: Leave-out markets only. The bot never came back to a secure area, so prep happens at the merchant instead and the set is already in position.

states.label: Powered on, health check
states.description: The deployment window opens and every bot in the set is powered on and checked. Each one comes out of this with a pass or a fail recorded, and nothing sits in between.

states.label: Tier 1 repair on the spot
states.description: Failed the check, but it is a tier 1 repair and the part is on hand. The health check re-runs before the bot goes anywhere. Where the tier 1 repair list is documented is still TBD.
states.rule: Never goes out on a failed check that was not fixed

states.label: Grounded
states.description: Not going out. Either the failure is beyond a tier 1 repair, the part is not on hand, or the bot grounded mid-route on the way to its merchant.

states.label: Awaiting pickup, inside
states.description: Held inside the private secure area for the pickup team, never staged on the sidewalk for a quick grab. What happens after the driver collects it is not documented in the SOP.
states.rule: Never visible from the public right of way

states.label: Clean, charged and ready
states.description: Passed the check, and cleaned and battery-swapped if last night was skipped. All of it inside the private secure area.
states.rule: Never prep or swap where the public can see it

states.label: Staged nose-in
states.description: Parked facing into the sidewalk so the pilot's first move is forward, with a dry departure path. Standing water on the path sends the bot back to be restaged rather than driven through.
states.rule: Never more than 2 bots staged together in the public right of way

states.label: Driving out under pilot
states.description: Trip sent and moving. The next pair does not leave until this one is out of sight, which is the rule that stops a line of bots forming on the sidewalk.
states.rule: Never more than 2 bots sent at a time

states.label: In service at the merchant
states.description: Deployed and working. This SOP ends here; the bot is now watched by the Regulatory Compliance model and comes home through the Undeployment model.
states.rule: Never more than 4 bots at any one merchant

transitions.label: Fails, tier 1 with the part on hand
Fails, not tier 1 or no part
Staged nose-in with a dry path
No dry path: restage
transitions.note: Standing water damages the base, so this is a hard stop rather than a judgement call.

transitions.label: Trip sent, two at a time
Out of sight, reaches the merchant
Grounds mid-route
transitions.note: Goes into the nearest private secure area, never the curb.
